claims.text: Increasing Mn concentration in magnetic high-entropy alloys will increase the coercive field.
The Mn-induced coercivity increase should occur at room temperature under standard conditions.
The spinel structure of high-entropy oxide nanoparticles is the structural mediator relevant to the proposed alloy response.
Increasing Mn concentration will increase spin frustration in the magnetic lattice.
A higher degree of spin frustration will produce a higher coercive field.
The Mn-enriched material will have a higher coercive field than an otherwise comparable material without the Mn increase.
There is a maximum Mn concentration that can be incorporated without changing the material's structure.
Mn concentration can be increased without changing the material's composition.
The relationship between Mn concentration and coercive field may depend on the specific alloy composition.
The relationship between Mn concentration and coercive field may depend on the synthesis method.
Coercive field and Mn concentration can be measured across samples with varying Mn concentration.
Failure of coercive field to increase with increasing Mn concentration would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: Increasing Mn concentration necessarily changes composition, whereas the boundary requires Mn incorporation without changing composition.

The target is described as a magnetic high-entropy alloy, but the proposed mediator is the spinel structure of high-entropy oxide nanoparticles, a different material class; no relationship between them is specified.
